project.name: Not Arbitrary 05 — The Bishop Is an Elephant

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: There is an elephant on your chessboard. It has been there fourteen hundred years, and you call it a bishop.
entries.direction: Warm, unhurried, opening a story. Land the last clause flat and plainly — it is the hook, not a joke.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: Chess begins in India, as a picture of an army. Foot soldiers, horses, chariots and elephants. Every piece is one of those four.
entries.direction: Conversational, as if sketching while speaking. Give each item of the four-item list its own small space so none of them runs into the next.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: The elephant was carved as an elephant, with a rider on its back. In Persian the word is pil. The Arabs made that al fil.
entries.direction: Matter of fact. Say pil as peel and al fil as al-feel, plainly, each finished before the next sentence begins. Do not carry any foreign colour into the English around them.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: Then the game crossed into lands where nobody carved living things. So a carver made the elephant without making an elephant. He kept the tusks and dropped the rest.
entries.direction: Slower, laying the cause down one step at a time. The last sentence is the whole mechanism — let it land.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: A block of ivory with two points on top. The same rule emptied the faces off a deck of playing cards.
entries.direction: Dry and flat on the first sentence. The second is an aside, thrown away lightly.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: Then it reaches Europe, where nobody knows the word or the animal. So every country guesses. England sees a bishop's hat. France sees a jester's cap and calls it the fool.
entries.direction: Brisker — this one moves. A small beat between each country's guess.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: Russia never had to guess. It has called that piece the elephant the whole time.
entries.direction: Quiet satisfaction. Short. Let the last phrase rest.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: The chariot went the same way. Everything gone but a notch in a block. And a notch in a block, to an Italian carver, is a wall you can shoot over.
entries.direction: Moving, slightly amused. The repeated phrase notch in a block is deliberate — do not rush past it the second time.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: So Europe put a castle on the board. England did not. It kept the Persian word for a chariot, and that word is rook. The only people who still say it think it means a castle.
entries.direction: Set the short sentences down cleanly with a pause after each, then open out on the last one. Say the word rook clearly and separately, rhyming with book, with a crisp r at the start of it.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: One piece never changed. A horse is a horse in every language around the board, so nobody had to guess.
entries.direction: Light and quick. Almost a shrug.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: The pieces crossed intact. The meanings did not. And one guess changed the game. The square beside the king never held a queen. It held the king's counsellor.
entries.direction: A turn. First two sentences flat and short, a pause, then the last two as a small provocation.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: He moved one square diagonally and nothing else. He was the weakest thing on the board for five hundred years. Europe had no viziers. Europe had queens.
entries.direction: Deliberate and dry. The final two sentences are the pivot of the film — even weight on both, no wink.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: So they called her a queen. And in Valencia somebody decided a queen should not be the weakest piece on the board. They gave her the chariot's line and the elephant's line.
entries.direction: Building, with real relish on the last sentence. Say Valencia the English way.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: Nothing on that board was designed. There is a foot soldier, a horse, a chariot, an elephant, and a civil servant wearing a crown.
entries.direction: Slower, laying each item of the list down separately with a clear space between them.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.text: You were never moving symbols. You were moving an army, out of a kingdom that fell before any of this was written down.
entries.direction: Warm close, slowing into the final line. Keep it simple and unhurried.
